passages.where: When the disciples say it might be better not to marry, Jesus names those who live unmarried for the sake of the kingdom, and says the one who can accept this should accept it. The site's note says he treats the capacity to live unmarried for the kingdom as a gift God gives, not an achievement or a duty laid on all, and that neither marriage nor celibacy is ranked as the higher way. Jesus, who was single, speaks of singleness here with honor.

Paul, himself unmarried, wants believers free from concern, and says the unmarried person is concerned with the work of the Lord while the married person's interests are divided. The site's plain note says his advice not to marry was not a law, that those who marry have not sinned, and that Paul honors both lives. Singleness here is a freedom with its own work to do, not an absence.

Paul tells every believer to lead the life the Lord has assigned and to which God has called them, and says he teaches this in all the churches. The site's note says the chapter urges each person to remain in the situation in which God called them. The life you have now is a place of calling, not a waiting room for the real one.

God speaks directly to eunuchs, men who could have no children and feared they would be cut off, and promises them a memorial in his house and a name better than sons and daughters. The site's note says the chapter's direction is unmistakable: faithfulness to God's covenant, not ancestry or bodily condition, defines his people. A life without marriage or children is not a life without a name before God.

Jesus promises that no one who has left home or family for his sake will fail to receive a hundredfold now, houses and brothers and sisters and mothers and children, along with persecutions. The site's plain note says these are the new family of believers who share their homes and lives. The church is meant to be that family in fact, not only in a sermon.

Told that his mother and brothers are outside, Jesus points to his disciples and says that whoever does his Father's will is his brother and sister and mother. The site's plain note says he is opening his family, not closing it. No one who belongs to him is without kin.

Paul tells Timothy to treat older men as fathers, younger men as brothers, older women as mothers and younger women as sisters, with absolute purity. The site's plain note heads the passage the church as a family. A congregation that lives this way gives every single person parents, siblings and children in the faith.

Jesus tells his disciples that he no longer calls them servants but friends, because he has made known to them everything he heard from the Father. The site's note says he defines the greatest love as laying down one's life for one's friends. Scripture's highest word about love is said of friendship, and it is open to every person, married or not.

Luke notes that Philip the evangelist had four unmarried daughters who prophesied. He says it in passing, as a plain fact about a household that served God. Single men and women stand throughout the New Testament as full members of the church and bearers of its word.

Heaven announces that the marriage of the Lamb has come, and an angel tells John to write that those invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb are blessed. The site's note says the chapter erupts in praise as the bride makes herself ready. Every human marriage points to this one, and every believer, married or single, is invited to it.

misread.taken: It is not good for the man to be alone is sometimes used to tell single people that their state is not good, that they are incomplete until they marry, or that they should marry whoever is available rather than stay single.
misread.says: The site's plain note on the chapter says that if you are single you are not half a person, since Jesus and Paul were single, and that if you are widowed or divorced, God has not set you aside. The note reads not good to be alone as God's compassion for every lonely person, and as the church's calling to be a family for them. The verse names a loneliness God answers, through marriage for many and through his people for all; it does not pronounce any single person unfinished.

whole: Singleness comes in many forms. Some have chosen it for God's sake. Many did not choose it, or have not chosen it yet, or are single again after loss or divorce, and some cannot marry for reasons they did not choose. For some it is a freedom they enjoy; for others it is a loneliness that sharpens at night and on holidays. Many single Christians know the small wounds of church life: the events built for couples and families, the friends who drift once they marry, the well-meant question about when, the sense of being a project for matchmakers, or of being trusted with less because they have no spouse. Some wonder whether God has passed them over, and some wonder whether wanting more than this is ingratitude.

Part of the weight is not from God at all. Many churches and cultures have quietly made marriage the measure of a finished adult life, and the site's notes say plainly that a church which treats single people as unfinished, or as a problem to be solved, has not listened to Jesus or to Paul. Some Christian traditions have erred the other way, treating a single life as holier than marriage, which Paul also refuses. Scripture's own picture is different from both. Jesus lived the fullest human life there has been unmarried. Paul called his singleness a gift. Isaiah promised childless believers a name better than sons and daughters. Most of us who are married, if we are honest, have made it harder for single friends by assuming their lives had not yet begun.

So the Bible's wisdom is to receive the life you have now as a calling, not a waiting room, whether or not you hope to marry. Paul's freedom for undivided devotion is real: time, attention and hospitality that married people often cannot give. Build deep friendships, which Scripture honors as a love in its own right. Belong to a church as family, not as a guest, and let it be family to you: people to eat with on ordinary nights, to call in trouble, to grow old beside. Keep your body in holiness, which is a calling for every Christian, married or not, and not a burden laid on single people alone. And if you long to marry, you can bring that longing to God honestly without letting it shrink the life in front of you.

The hope Scripture gives is not that every single person will marry, but that no one who belongs to Christ is without kin or without a name. Jesus calls his followers friends and gives them brothers, sisters, mothers and children a hundredfold in his family. Every human marriage points beyond itself to the marriage supper of the Lamb, and every believer is invited to that table, married or single. A single life lived for God is not a smaller life. It may be, as Jesus and Paul showed, one of the clearest pictures there is of what every life is finally for.

differ.share: Christians agree that singleness for the kingdom is a calling to be honored, not a lesser life; that it is a gift some are given, not a rule for everyone; that those who marry do not sin; and that the church is to be a family for every believer.

views.name: Celibacy for the kingdom, and vowed life
views.body: The Catholic Church teaches that priests of the Latin Church are normally chosen from men who live celibate lives for the sake of the kingdom of heaven, and it honors vowed religious life.

views.name: Married priests and celibate bishops
views.body: The Orthodox churches ordain married men as priests and choose their bishops from among the celibate.

views.name: Not everyone can accept this word
views.body: Protestant churches have stressed Jesus' words that not everyone can accept this saying; the Augsburg Confession of 1530 cited them against requiring all clergy to stay unmarried.

differ.after: The site's notes on Matthew 19 set out these practices and do not choose between them. Each honors a single life given to God, and none treats it as a lesser one.

sit: If your single life is a calling now and not only a season to get through, what is it calling you to give, and whom is it calling you to belong to?

prayer.lead: Moses' prayer to be satisfied each morning with God's loving devotion and to have the work of his hands established. Pray it over the life you have now.

careLines.text: This passage does not ask you to explain yourself.
A church that treats single people as unfinished, or as a problem to be solved, has not listened to him.
If you are single, you are not half a person: Jesus and Paul were single.
